CreateHistoricalReachCurveRequestContent.description: Request to generate a historical reach curve.

endDate.description: The end date for the curve data. This is in the ISO 8601 format. For example 2023-01-31.

startDate.description: The start date for the curve data. This is in the ISO 8601 format. For example 2023-01-01.

targeting.description: A list of dimensions that build the targeting expression that is used for generating a reach curve.

totalResults.description: The total number of data points.

HistoricalReachCurveDataPoint.description: A data point in the Reach Curve for Historical data.

channel.description: Supply package for which the reach curve has been generated.

demographic.description: The demographic segment applied to the reach curve.

endDate.description: The end of the time window the reach curve is based on.

impressions.description: The number of ads that were delivered.

reachType.description: The type of reach, for example INDIVIDUALS or HOUSEHOLDS.

startDate.description: The beginning of the time window the reach curve is based on.

endDate.description: The format of the date is YYYY-MM-DD.

startDate.description: The format of the date is YYYY-MM-DD.

channels.description: List of channels that were used for showing the ads.

demographics.description: List of demographics of the audience that are represented in the data.

geography.description: Name of the locale/geography that the metadata belongs to.

reachTypes.description: List of the different reach types available to request.

geography.description: The locales/geographies that the metadata belongs to.

month.description: The month that the metadata belongs to in the format MM/YYYY.

metadata.description: List of Historical Reach Curves metadata separated by geography.

month.description: The month that this data belongs to.

maxResults.description: Number of records to include in the paginated response. Defaults to 1000.

month.description: The month of data that will be returned. Defaults to the most recent month of data that is available for the given geography.

nextToken.description: Token to retrieve the next set/page of data points.

historicalReachCurves.description: List of data points for a curve that shows historical reach. The default list size is 1000 data points.

nextToken.description: The token to retrieve the next set/page of data points.

totalResults.description: Total available data points for the requested resource.

ReachFrequency.description: The frequency of exposures to households or individuals.

fivePlus.description: Number of ads viewed at least five times.

fourPlus.description: Number of ads viewed at least four times.

onePlus.description: Number of ads viewed at least once.

sixPlus.description: Number of ads viewed at least six times.

threePlus.description: Number of ads viewed at least thrice.

twoPlus.description: Number of ads viewed at least twice.

channels.description: The mode that ads were delivered. For example "STV" and "Prime_Video".

demographics.description: The demographic segments of the users included in the reach curve.

geography.description: The geography of the users included in the reach curve.

reachType.description: The type of reach recorded for the data. Possible values are "INDIVIDUALS" and "HOUSEHOLDS".

dimensionGroups.description:
A list of targeting dimensions that allows you to have nested targeting dimensions. Typically, you will only
use this for the `audienceId` dimension.

dimensionName.description:
The name of the dimension you are targeting.

The available dimension names are:
| Dimension Name | Allowed Dimension Types |
|----------------|-------------------------|
| `supplyPackage` | `SINGLE` |
| `demographic` | `SINGLE` |
| `reachType` | `SINGLE` |
| `geography` | `SINGLE` |
| `frequencyThreshold` | `SINGLE` |
| `audienceId` | `SINGLE`, `MULTIPLE`, `GROUP` |

The following table contains certain dimensions and their corresponding possible values.
| Dimension Name | Description | Available Dimension Values |
|----------------|-------------|----------------------------|
| supplyPackage | The supply source of the data that will generate the reach curve. | 'STV' |
| reachType | Whether the targeted audience are individuals or households. | 'INDIVIDUALS', 'HOUSEHOLDS' |
| geography | The location for which to generate a reach curve. | 'US' |
| frequencyThreshold | The minimum number of times an ad was shown. | '1', '2', '3', '4', '5', '6' |
| audienceId | The ID of an audience that is targeted to generate the reach curve. | |
| demographic | The demographic that is targeted to generate the reach curve. | |.

dimensionValue.description: The value of the dimension you are targeting.

dimensionValues.description:
A list of values of the dimension you are targeting.
The max limit varies on the dimension name.

isNot.description: Whether to negate this dimension or not.

CreateHistoricalReachCurve_example1.summary: Example of generating US historical reach curve using one audience ID and a demographic type.

CreateHistoricalReachCurve_example2.summary: Example of generating US historical reach curve using multiple audience IDs and one demographic type.

CreateHistoricalReachCurve_example3.description:
This example shows you how to use the `dimensionType` of `group`. Notice how, when a single audience ID is to be negated, a dimension type of group is used so you can add
        multiple dimensions within it. The dimension with type of `group` sets the `intraOperator` to `OR`, which implies that all the dimension groups within the `dimensionGroups` list will be OR'd against each other.
        The first dimension group is of type `single` so that you can set just that audience ID to be negated. The next group sets the `interOperator` to `OR` so that each audience ID within the list of `dimensionValues` is OR'd against each other.
.
CreateHistoricalReachCurve_example3.summary: Example of generating US historical reach curve using multiple audience segments (with one negated) and one demographic type. This example will show you how to use the `dimensionType` of `group`.
